target_customer: Crypto users wanting a self-custody wallet with a spendable Visa card, later businesses and stablecoin payments
problem: Crypto holders could not easily spend assets from their own wallet at ordinary merchants without trusting a custodial exchange card.
business_model: Card fees and subscription plans (premium plan reported at $199 per year), interchange, token incentives
product_category: Non-custodial crypto wallet and card issuing

founders.name: Kuberan Marimuthu
founders.background_notes: YC bio says he sold Cypher to Nium after reaching $5M annualized revenue.

exit.reason: Nium bought the wallet and issuing business; consumer app, cards and CYPR ecosystem wind down with shutdown on 2026-09-06.

technical_complexity.rationale: Multichain non-custodial wallet plus card issuing partnerships and token conversion at point of sale; mostly integration work with some compliance dependency.

defensibility.rationale: Card issuing relied on partners and exchange cards from Crypto.com and Coinbase were large alternatives; little lock-in.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Exchange cards remained dominant; Cypher survived to 2026 and sold to Nium, which is shutting the consumer products.

market_need_then: Demand for spending crypto existed in 2021 and 2022 through exchange cards, but self-custody card options were few; no dated source quantified demand.

branding.brand_signature: Self-custody card pitched as the first zero-fee crypto card (company claim)
branding.community_and_virality: Active Discord, Telegram, X and Reddit channels plus a CYPR token and rewards program; no merch or press on the brand found.

brand_strength.rationale: Real community channels and token, but the word Cypher is generic and shared with other crypto projects.

pivots.from: Consumer multichain wallet and crypto card
pivots.to: Business card platform and stablecoin payments focus
pivots.why: The site lists Business and Agent Pay products and Nium's deal targets B2B stablecoin use cases.

outcome_analysis: Cypher raised a $4.3M YC-led seed in January 2023 and, per the founder, reached $5M annualized revenue selling a self-custody Visa card. In July 2026 Nium acquired the wallet and issuing business at an undisclosed price while the consumer app, cards and CYPR token program were wound down by September 2026. The outcome looks like a technology and licence pickup rather than a consumer success, though terms are unknown.
notes: Seed date conflicts: The Block 2023-01-19, another profile June 2023, VCBacked March 2022. CB Insights shows $4.8M over 5 rounds, unverified. Competitor searches returned only current card guides, so no dated competitors were recorded. Founded year per YC is 2021 though one source says 2022. Acquisition and shutdown dates from Cypher's own site and Nium coverage. The founder bio claim of $5M annualized revenue is self-reported.
